caveats: Research method limit: WebFetch failed with DNS errors on every domain (including en.wikipedia.org), and curl got proxy 403. Every price here comes from search-engine extracts of UK retailer pages, not from a live page load. The extracts are machine summaries, so a figure may be mis-transcribed or stale. Open each URL to confirm before relying on it.
'observedAt' is the research date (2026-10-18). The date the search engine indexed each page is unknown and may be months earlier. One listing (Carlton Services) was flagged as about 262 days old.

The shared web-search budget (200 calls across all agents in this run) ran out after 7 searches by this agent. Panasonic (TZ, Etherea), Daikin Stylish, Daikin 2MXM/3MXM/4MXM, Mitsubishi MSZ-HR, MSZ-LN, MXZ, and the 2.5/5.0 kW sizes for Sensira and MSZ-AP were NOT researched. They have no observations, and their summary rows are null.

Panasonic: the only UK distributor seen (Oceanair UK, e.g. https://www.oceanairuk.com/products/panasonic-etherea-cu-z35zke-single-split-outdoor-unit-r32-3-5kw) hides prices behind a trade login; its listing says the outdoor unit must be installed by an F-gas certified installer. All other Panasonic prices found were EU (EUR) retailers, which are not recorded here.

Generations: several observed models may be superseded or end-of-line. Daikin Perfera FTXM-R has an FTXM-A successor (see docs/research/data/daikin.json). Orion says MSZ-AP35VGK is replaced by MSZ-AY35VGK. Sensira listings mix D/E/F suffixes. Prices for current-generation units may differ. Confirm the shippable model code with the distributor.

F-gas: no extract said whether a site limits sales to F-gas certified buyers, so every observation records it as not determinable. Background (not verified in this session): GB F-gas rules restrict selling non-hermetically-sealed split equipment to end users unless certified installation is evidenced, so expect online sellers to ask for an F-gas / REFCOM certificate number or installer details at checkout. Fact-check 2026-10-18: still UNVERIFIED (legislation.gov.uk unreachable, search budget exhausted). The provision this is believed to rest on is Article 11(5) of Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 as retained in GB law (non-hermetically sealed equipment charged with F-gases sold to an end user only with evidence that a certified undertaking will install it). docs/research/commissioning-standards.md also grades this unverified. Confirm the current GB text at https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/517/contents and check for any 2025-2026 GB F-gas amendment before building a checkout or purchasing rule on it.

'isPairKit' is inferred from titles and price levels for Avon Air (MSZ-AP35VGK), Orion (MSZ-AP35VGK), SWAT Engineering and Carlton Services; their titles name only the indoor model. 'Install Kit' listings (Orion, Tiedex) are not defined in the extracts and are kept out of the plain-pair ranges.

VAT: vatIncluded=null means the extract did not show the VAT treatment; those rows are left out of the summary ranges. Where an inc-VAT price was the only figure, ex-VAT = price/1.2 (20% UK standard rate). Supply-only equipment bought by a VAT-registered installer carries 20% VAT; the 0% domestic rate for energy-saving materials applies to installed supply, not to equipment the trade buys. Fact-check 2026-10-18: CONFIRMED in substance against VATA 1994 Sch 8 Group 23 Item 2 ('Relevant supplies of energy-saving materials by a person who installs those materials', https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/23/schedule/8/part/II/group/23, as quoted in docs/research/uk-consumer-legal.md). Three qualifications: (1) the 0% rate covers supplies made before 1 April 2027, and 5% applies from 1 April 2027 (Sch 7A Group 2, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/23/schedule/7A/part/2/group/2), so Rimy's 'VAT-free for domestic customers' is time-limited; (2) whether an air-to-air unit counts as an 'air source heat pump' rests on HMRC's VENSAV3080 view as quoted by secondary sources; (3) supply-only equipment carries 20% VAT whoever buys it, and VAT registration only decides whether the installer can recover it.

These are public retail/e-commerce prices. Trade account prices from distributors (e.g. Climate Center, Oceanair, Wolseley, City Plumbing trade) are usually lower and were not captured. Do not treat these figures as the installer's cost price.

Fact-check 2026-10-18, claims CONFIRMED by cross-checking other repo research (secondary, not live): Perfera FTXM-R has an FTXM-A successor (daikin.json cites Daikin UK FTXM-A pages and 2025 Lot 10 labels); FTXM35R is multi-split capable (Daikin Lot 10 fiche FTXM20R5V1B / FTXM35R5V1B / 2MXM40A2V1B9 in daikin.json); Sensira FTXF-E/D are older than FTXF-F (daikin.json); MSZ-AP 'VGK' units have built-in Wi-Fi and MSZ-AY replaces MSZ-AP at 2.5-5.0 kW in the UK (mitsubishi.json); Panasonic has no GBP price anywhere in the repo, so its rows stay null (panasonic.json). All ex-VAT figures, inc/ex pairs and summary min/max/n were recomputed and match.

Capacity and btu labels: the kW and btu figures in 'description' are retailer size-class labels, not rated capacities. Examples: Daikin's FTXF35F nominal cooling is 3.3 kW against a 3.5 kW label design capacity (daikin.json); Micro-Climate titles FTXM35R as '3.4 kW'; '18,000 btu' for 5.0 kW is about 5.5% above the converted 17,060 btu/h. Take capacities from daikin.json or mitsubishi.json, not from this file.
